blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Mastery of All Domains
blocks.content: Tatsavit is the final boss of the Tenali math platform. It is not a topic; it is a brutal, high-speed test of every single concept you have learned. It demands rapid context-switching, deep conceptual understanding, and perfect execution under pressure. This is where you prove you are a true math warrior.

blocks.title: 2. The Strategy: Mind Over Panic
blocks.content: When facing a mix of geometry, algebra, statistics, and probability questions back-to-back, your brain will try to panic. The key is to take a 2-second breath before every question. Identify the topic first. Load the specific rules for that topic into your working memory, THEN start calculating.

blocks.title: 3. The Method: Triage
blocks.content:
In a timed, mixed exam:

1. Do the immediate, 10-second questions first (like basic indices or evaluating functions).
2. If a question looks like a 3-minute slog, flag it and move on.
3. Secure the easy points to build a safety net.
4. Return to the flagged monsters with the remaining time.

blocks.title: 4. The Ultimate Advice: Read Carefully
blocks.content: In high-level tests, the math is often easy, but the wording is a trap. 'Find the radius' vs 'Find the diameter'. 'Nearest tenth' vs 'Nearest whole number'. 'Increase by 20%' vs 'Decrease by 20%'. Under pressure, your eyes will lie to you. Read every question twice.

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The biggest pitfall in Tatsavit is losing your confidence after one hard question. If you stare at a probability question for 2 minutes and get it wrong, you carry that frustration into the next algebra question, causing you to make a simple sign error. You must develop a goldfish memory. When a question is done, forget it instantly and attack the next one fresh.
